tagline: A short loop through a valley the meltwater cut.
intro: The byway is a 36-mile loop through the corners of O'Brien, Clay, Buena Vista and Cherokee counties, around the small towns of Peterson and Linn Grove. Surging glacial meltwater cut the middle valley of the Little Sioux River deep into soft drift, and steep hills of unplowed prairie now stand along the meandering river above its forested and farmed bottoms.

The Prairie Heritage Center near Peterson explains what the ice left behind, kames and kettles, glacial till, hanging valleys and catsteps. Artifacts of the Mill Creek culture here go back to around 1000 AD.

moments.title: Peterson
moments.text: Settlers built a fort here in 1862 against a Dakota attack that never came, and its blockhouse still stands near where it was built, at Second and Park.

moments.title: Linn Grove
moments.text: The town is named for a grove of linden trees and lies near the Chan-Ya-Ta Site, the remains of a prehistoric village a thousand years old.
